s: According to the Brundtland definition, sustainable development balances present needs with which of the following?
o: the ability of future generations to meet their own needs
a ban on present use of natural resources
x: Sustainable development meets present needs while preserving future generations' ability to meet theirs; it does not prohibit resource use.

s: What is the basic goal of sustainable development?
o: Maximise economic growth for the present generation
Halt economic development to conserve resources
Meet present needs while preserving choices for future generations
Restrict present consumption to subsistence for future needs
x: The core goal is to meet present needs without reducing the options available to future generations, within the Earth's carrying capacity.

s: Which of the following is NOT a goal of sustainable development?
x: Profit maximisation is a growth-centric aim; sustainable development seeks equity across generations within carrying capacity.

s: Sustainable development seeks a balance among which three pillars?
o: Environmental protection, population control and conservation
Economic growth, social inclusion and environmental protection
Social inclusion, poverty reduction and employment
x: Sustainable development balances economic growth, social inclusion and environmental protection rather than maximising any one pillar alone.

s: Which of the following is one of the three pillars of sustainability?
x: The three pillars are economic growth, social inclusion or equity, and environmental protection.

s: On which date was Agenda 2030 for Sustainable Development adopted in New York?
x: Agenda 2030 was adopted on 25 September 2015 in New York.

s: What are the two principal roots of Agenda 2030?
o: The World Trade Organization and the International Monetary Fund
The Kyoto Protocol and the Montreal Protocol
The Millennium Development Goals and the Rio+20 outcome
The Stockholm Convention and the Paris Agreement
x: Agenda 2030 grew from the Millennium Development Goals and the outcome of the Rio+20 Conference.

s: In which year was Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) launched?
x: Mission LiFE was launched in 2021 to change consumption and production behaviour.

s: What is the principle that Agenda 2030 applies to developed, developing and least developed countries alike known as?
x: Universality means that Agenda 2030 applies to all countries, irrespective of their level of development.

s: How many goals did the Millennium Development Goals have?
x: The MDGs had 8 goals for 2000-2015; the SDGs have 17.

s: Under the 'leave no one behind' principle of Agenda 2030, by what is progress measured?
o: The poorest and most excluded groups
x: Leave no one behind measures progress by the poorest and most excluded, not by averages.

s: In which of the following is Agenda 2030 grounded?
x: Agenda 2030 is grounded in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, human rights treaties, the Millennium Declaration and the 2005 World Summit Outcome.

s: What was the period of the Millennium Development Goals?
x: The 8 MDGs ran from 2000 to 2015; the SDGs followed for 2016-2030.

s: The three health-related Millennium Development Goals were merged into which Sustainable Development Goal?
x: MDG 4 (child mortality), MDG 5 (maternal health) and MDG 6 (HIV/malaria) were merged into SDG 3.

s: How many of the eight Millennium Development Goals were related to health?
x: Three of the eight MDGs (4, 5 and 6) dealt with health.

s:
Consider the following statements about Agenda 2030:
1. Its 17 goals are integrated and indivisible and are to be pursued together.
2. It applies only to developing and least developed countries.
3. It is also informed by the Declaration on the Right to Development.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Agenda 2030 is integrated and indivisible and informed by the Declaration on the Right to Development; it is universal, so statement 2 is wrong.

s: How many targets are there under the 17 Sustainable Development Goals of Agenda 2030?
x: The 17 SDGs carry 169 targets (APPSC-GS 2025 key). 99, 129 and 150 are distractors and do not match any SDG count.

s: How many unique global indicators are there for the SDGs?
x: The SDGs have 17 goals, 169 targets and 231 unique global indicators; 277 is India's National Indicator Framework 2026.

s: What does SDG 14 deal with?
x: SDG 14 is Life below water; SDG 15 is Life on land and SDG 13 Climate action.

s: Which Sustainable Development Goal has the theme of clean water and sanitation?
x: SDG 6 is clean water and sanitation; SDG 7 is affordable and clean energy.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: SDG 5 is Gender equality; SDG 2 is Zero hunger, SDG 4 Quality education and SDG 15 Life on land.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Goal)
A. SDG 7
B. SDG 11
C. SDG 13
D. SDG 15
List-II (Theme)
1. Climate action
2. Life on land
3. Affordable and clean energy
4. Sustainable cities and communities
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: SDG 7 = affordable and clean energy, SDG 11 = sustainable cities, SDG 13 = climate action, SDG 15 = life on land.

s: Which Sustainable Development Goal deals with climate action?
x: SDG 13 is climate action; SDG 14 is life below water and SDG 15 is life on land.

s: What is the title of the Brundtland Commission report (1987) that defined sustainable development?
x: The Brundtland report, Our Common Future (1987), defined sustainable development.

s: The decision to develop the Sustainable Development Goals was taken at which event?
x: The 2012 Rio+20 Conference, formally the United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development, took the decision to develop the SDGs.

s: Which body is credited with the first formal definition of sustainable development?
o: World Commission on Environment and Development
x: The World Commission on Environment and Development (Brundtland Commission) first defined sustainable development in Our Common Future.

s: In which year was the World Summit on Sustainable Development (Rio+10) held in Johannesburg?
x: The Johannesburg World Summit of 2002 reviewed progress ten years after Rio.

s: Which body was created as a result of the 1972 Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment?
x: Stockholm 1972 first put the environment on the global agenda and created UNEP.

s: Where was the UN Conference on the Human Environment held in 1972?
x: The 1972 UN Conference on the Human Environment was held in Stockholm and created UNEP.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Report)
A. Limits to Growth
B. Our Common Future
C. World Conservation Strategy
List-II (Prepared by)
1. WCED
2. Club of Rome
3. IUCN, UNEP and WWF
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Limits to Growth (1972) was by the Club of Rome, Our Common Future (1987) by the WCED, and the World Conservation Strategy (1980) by IUCN, UNEP and WWF.

s: At which conference was Agenda 21 adopted?
x: Agenda 21, the first global plan of action for sustainable development, came out of the Rio Earth Summit (UNCED) of 1992.

s: In which year was the Club of Rome founded?
x: The Club of Rome was founded in April 1968; it brought out 'Limits to Growth' in 1972.

s: In which city was the Club of Rome founded in April 1968?
x: It began as a meeting at the Accademia dei Lincei in Rome in April 1968.

s: Which of the following was an outcome of the UN Conference on Environment and Development (Rio, 1992)?
x: Rio 1992 produced the Rio Declaration, Agenda 21 and the UNFCCC; UNEP came from Stockholm 1972.

s: Who chaired the Brundtland Commission?
x: The World Commission on Environment and Development was chaired by Gro Harlem Brundtland, who was the Prime Minister of Norway.

s: What is the title of the Brundtland Report of 1987?
x: 'Our Common Future' (1987) is the Brundtland Report; 'Limits to Growth' is the Club of Rome's 1972 report.

s: Gro Harlem Brundtland, who chaired the WCED, was the Prime Minister of which country?
x: Gro Harlem Brundtland was Prime Minister of Norway, not Sweden.

s: In which year was the Brundtland Commission set up by the UN General Assembly?
x: The WCED (Brundtland Commission) was set up by the UN General Assembly in 1983; its report came in 1987.

s: How many indicators are there in India's National Indicator Framework 2026 released by MoSPI?
x: MoSPI's National Indicator Framework 2026 (1 July 2026) has 277 indicators.

s: Which of the following pairs about India in the SDSN Sustainable Development Report 2026 is correctly matched?
o: Neighbour India ranked ahead of – Bhutan
x: India ranked 94th, behind Bhutan, Maldives, Nepal and Sri Lanka, lagged on 13 SDGs, and SDG 2 was its main concern.

s: In the SDSN Sustainable Development Report 2025, India entered the top 100 for the first time. What was its rank?
x: India ranked 99th out of 167 with a score of about 67 in 2025.

s: In which year did India present its first Voluntary National Review on the SDGs to the UN?
x: India's first VNR was in 2017 and covered 7 SDGs; NITI Aayog prepared the VNR 2025.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: SDG India Index 2023-24 — Andhra Pradesh, score 79
SDG India Index 2023-24 — Bihar, highest score
SDG India Index 2023-24 — Kerala and Uttarakhand, score 57
x: India's national score in the SDG India Index 2023-24 was 71. Kerala and Uttarakhand scored 79, while Bihar scored 57.

s: In NITI Aayog's SDG India Index 2023-24, which States topped with a score of 79?
x: Kerala and Uttarakhand topped with 79; India scored 71 and Bihar was last with 57.

s: India's first Voluntary National Review (2017) covered how many SDGs?
x: India's first VNR in 2017 covered 7 SDGs: 1, 2, 3, 5, 9, 14 and 17.

s: What was India's rank in the Sustainable Development Report 2026?
x: India ranked 94th in 2026, 18 places better than in 2015; it first entered the top 100 in 2025.

s: Which body publishes the Sustainable Development Report that ranks countries on the SDGs?
x: The Sustainable Development Report is published by the UN SDSN; its lead author is Jeffrey Sachs.

s: Which body coordinates the Sustainable Development Goals in India?
x: NITI Aayog coordinates the SDGs in India; MoSPI builds the National Indicator Framework used to measure them.

s: Which country topped the SDSN Sustainable Development Report 2025?
x: Finland topped the SDR 2025, followed by Sweden and Denmark; India was 99th of 167.

s: Who is the lead author of the Sustainable Development Report published by the UN SDSN?
x: The SDSN's Sustainable Development Report is led by Jeffrey Sachs.

s: Which State scored the lowest (57) in NITI Aayog's SDG India Index 2023-24?
x: In the SDG India Index 2023-24, Bihar was last with 57; Kerala and Uttarakhand topped with 79.

s: Which edition of NITI Aayog's SDG India Index was the 2023-24 index released in July 2024?
x: The SDG India Index 2023-24 (July 2024) was the 4th edition.

s: Which body builds the National Indicator Framework used to measure India's progress on the SDGs?
x: NITI Aayog coordinates the SDGs, while MoSPI builds the National Indicator Framework.

s: With which SDG is the Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs proposed in Amaravati under the MoU with UN-Habitat primarily aligned?
x: The Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs is aligned with SDG 11, which concerns sustainable cities and communities.

s: Andhra Pradesh's SDG monitoring and reporting framework is part of which system of the Planning Department?
x: AP's SDG framework is part of ROMS of the Planning Department, with indicators tracked at state, district and secretariat levels.

s: Which body runs district monitoring and real-time dashboards for the Swarna Andhra @2047 vision?
x: The AP State Development Planning Society (APSDPS) of the Planning Department runs them.

s: Where is the headquarters of UN-Habitat, with which Andhra Pradesh signed an MoU in July 2026 for a Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs in Amaravati?
x: UN-Habitat has its headquarters in Nairobi.

s: Which of the following principles was NOT endorsed at the 1992 Rio process?
x: The precautionary principle, polluter pays principle and common but differentiated responsibilities were endorsed at Rio 1992. Unrestricted resource exploitation is contrary to sustainable development.

s: What is the principle that lack of full scientific certainty is no reason to postpone action against serious environmental damage called?
x: This is the precautionary principle endorsed at Rio 1992.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Rio 1992 principles:
1. The polluter pays principle was endorsed.
2. Common but differentiated responsibilities was endorsed.
3. Unrestricted resource exploitation was endorsed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Polluter pays and CBDR were endorsed at Rio; unrestricted resource exploitation goes against sustainable development and was not.

s: Under the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities (CBDR), why do developed countries carry a larger share of responsibility?
o: Because of their historical emissions and greater capacity
Because they hold most of the world's forests
Because they signed the Rio Declaration first
x: CBDR: all countries share responsibility, but developed countries carry more because of historical emissions and greater capacity.

s: What is the maximum population an environment can support indefinitely without degradation called?
x: Carrying capacity is the maximum population that an environment can support indefinitely without degradation.

s: What is the date on which humanity's annual demand on nature exceeds what the Earth can regenerate that year called?
x: Earth Overshoot Day marks the point when humanity's demand on nature in a year exceeds what the Earth can regenerate during that year.

s: Which organisation computes Earth Overshoot Day?
x: Earth Overshoot Day is computed yearly by the Global Footprint Network, not UNEP.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 — protection of wildlife and habitats and regulation of hunting
Water Act, 1974 — control of air pollution only
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 — creation of the Pollution Control Boards
x: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 protects wildlife and habitats and regulates hunting. The other purposes are associated with different laws.

s: In which year did the Ganga Action Plan begin?
x: The Ganga Action Plan began in 1986; 1982 is the incorrect year associated with it.

s: Under which Act is Environmental Impact Assessment mandatory?
o: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
x: Environmental Impact Assessment is mandatory under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.

s: Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) provisions fall under which legislation?
o: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act
x: Coastal Regulation Zone provisions fall under the Environment (Protection) Act.

s: Under which Act was the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) constituted in 1974 as a statutory body?
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act
Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act
x: CPCB was set up in 1974 under the Water Act and later got functions under the Air Act, 1981. The EP Act came only in 1986, and the Wildlife Act (1972) does not deal with pollution boards.

s: In which year was the Air Act of 1981 amended with stricter penalties?
x: The Air Act, 1981 was amended in 1987.

s: Which Act is the umbrella law for environmental protection in India?
x: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is the umbrella law; EIA and CRZ fall under it.

s: In which year was the Forest (Conservation) Act enacted?
x: The Forest (Conservation) Act dates from 1980.

s: Under which section of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 were the Environmental Protection Fund Rules, 2026 made?
x: The Environmental Protection Fund Rules, 2026 come under Section 16 of the EP Act and pool fines collected under three Acts.

s: In August 2025, under which provisions did the Supreme Court hold that State Pollution Control Boards can levy compensation?
o: Section 33A of the Water Act and Section 31A of the Air Act
Sections 3 and 5 of the Environment (Protection) Act
x: The SC (Aug 2025) traced SPCB compensation powers to Sec. 33A of the Water Act and Sec. 31A of the Air Act.

s: What is the logo of the Eco-Mark scheme (1991)?
x: The Eco-Mark logo is an earthen pot; products are certified by the BIS, not the CPCB.

s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board classification, what are 'White' category industries?
x: White-category industries are practically non-polluting; Green-category industries have low pollution potential.

s: Which body certifies products under the Eco-Mark scheme?
x: Eco-Mark is certified by the Bureau of Indian Standards, not the CPCB.

s: Which of the following product categories is NOT covered by the Eco-Mark scheme?
x: Eco-Mark covers soaps, detergents, paper, cosmetics and more, but not drugs or antibiotics.

s: Under which Act was the Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board constituted on 24 January 1976?
x: APPCB was constituted in 1976 under the Water Act; its air role came in 1981.

s: What is EPTRI, Hyderabad, an institution for?
x: EPTRI does environment training and research; Eco-Mark is certified by BIS.

s: In which year was the Eco-Mark scheme launched?
x: The Eco-Mark scheme for environment-friendly products was launched in 1991; its logo is an earthen pot.

s: In the context of the precautionary principle, on whom does the burden of proving that an activity is benign rest?
o: The person or entity undertaking the activity
x: Under the precautionary principle, the burden of proof shifts to the actor undertaking the potentially harmful activity to demonstrate that it is benign.

s: Under the Polluter Pays Principle, what does the polluter bear?
o: the costs of remediation and compensation for damage
only private compensation claimed by victims
no cost, as liability shifts to the State
x: The principle covers both remediation of environmental damage and compensation for those affected.

s: Which principle holds that the State holds natural resources in trust for the public?
x: The public trust doctrine treats the State as trustee of natural resources for the public.

s: To whom does the principle of absolute liability apply?
o: The State, as trustee of natural resources
Any actor, until the activity is proved harmless
x: Absolute liability applies to hazardous industries with no exceptions.

s: The Ratlam Municipality judgment is associated with which of the following?
o: Municipal duty to address public nuisance
Mandatory use of CNG in Delhi
x: Ratlam Municipality (1980) recognised the municipal duty to deal with public nuisance and protect public health and sanitation.

s: With which of the following is the Taj Trapezium case associated?
o: chemical units in Rajasthan paying for clean-up
the State holding natural resources in trust
the right to pollution-free water and air under Article 21
x: The Taj Trapezium case mandated CNG; the Rajasthan chemical units clean-up was the Bichhri case.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum case – Precautionary principle only
Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum case – Polluter Pays Principle only
Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum case – Precautionary and Polluter Pays principles
Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum case – Tannery pollution of the Ganga
x: The Vellore case, on tannery pollution of the Palar River, applied both the precautionary and Polluter Pays principles.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Precautionary principle — Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum v Union of India
Public trust doctrine — M.C. Mehta v Kamal Nath
Absolute liability — M.C. Mehta v Kamal Nath
Polluter pays — Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v Union of India
x: Absolute liability is associated with M.C. Mehta v Union of India in the Oleum gas leak case. M.C. Mehta v Kamal Nath is associated with the public trust doctrine.

s: The Oleum gas case (M.C. Mehta, 1986) laid down which doctrine?
x: The Oleum gas leak case of 1986 laid down absolute liability.

s: With which of the following is M.C. Mehta v Kamal Nath (1997) associated?
x: Kamal Nath (1997) applied the public trust doctrine; the Taj Trapezium case mandated CNG.

s: Which principle did the Bichhri case (1996), on Rajasthan chemical units, apply?
o: Both the precautionary and Polluter Pays principles
x: Bichhri applied only the Polluter Pays Principle; Vellore applied both principles.

s: Which case held that 'forest' covers all forests regardless of ownership?
x: In T.N. Godavarman (1995) the Supreme Court read 'forest' to cover all forests, whoever owns them.

s: The Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum case (1996) concerned tannery pollution of which river?
x: The Vellore case dealt with tanneries polluting the Palar in Tamil Nadu and applied the precautionary and polluter pays principles.

s: Which of the following is NOT a mission under the NAPCC?
x: The eight NAPCC missions include Solar, Sustainable Agriculture and Green India; Coastal Security is not one of them.

s: In which year was the National Action Plan on Climate Change, with eight national missions, released?
x: NAPCC came in 2008 with eight missions; 2006 is the National Environment Policy year.

s: Which of the following is one of the eight missions under the NAPCC?
x: Green India is a NAPCC mission; Coastal Security is a known trap.

s: Which Article makes protection of the environment a duty of the State as a Directive Principle?
x: Article 48A (DPSP) is the State's duty; Article 51A(g) is the citizen's Fundamental Duty.

s: Which case read the right to pollution-free water and air into Article 21?
x: Subhash Kumar v Bihar (1991) read pollution-free water and air into Article 21.

s:
Consider the following statements about constitutional provisions on the environment:
1. Article 48A is a Fundamental Duty of the citizen.
2. Article 51A(g) is a Fundamental Duty of the citizen.
3. Article 21 has been read to include a clean environment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Article 48A is a DPSP, a duty of the State; 51A(g) and the Article 21 reading are correct.

s: In which year was the National Environment Policy adopted?
x: The National Environment Policy was adopted in 2006 and serves as India’s overarching environment policy.

s: What is the central idea of the National Environment Policy, 2006?
o: Economic growth must always be stopped to protect natural resources
Conservation and livelihood security are mutually exclusive
Environmental protection should be separated from development planning
Conservation and livelihood security can proceed together
x: The NEP 2006 rests on the idea that conservation and livelihood security go together rather than being opposed to each other.

s: Which of the following doctrines is listed among the principles of the National Environment Policy, 2006, along with the precautionary approach and polluter pays?
x: NEP 2006 rests on the precautionary approach, polluter pays and the public trust doctrine. Eminent domain, pith and substance and laches are land-acquisition, federal and equity doctrines, not NEP principles.

s: Which of the following is an objective of the National Environment Policy, 2006?
o: Elimination of all development activity in ecologically sensitive areas
Keeping environmental concerns out of development plans
Halting all use of critical environmental resources
Integration of environmental concerns into development plans
x: NEP 2006 seeks to integrate environmental concerns into development plans; it does not prescribe ending all development in sensitive areas.

s: For which type of projects was Environmental Impact Assessment first used in India in 1978?
x: EIA was first used in 1978 for river valley projects.

s: In which year was the EIA notification, first issued in 1994, revised?
x: The EIA notification of 1994 was revised in 2006.

s: Which authority clears Category B projects under the EIA notification?
x: Category B projects are cleared by the State SEIAA; Category A by the MoEFCC.

s: Which is the correct order of the stages of EIA?
x: EIA runs screening, scoping, public consultation and then appraisal.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Draft EIA 2020?
o: It drew controversy over environmental safeguards
It raised the public notice period from 20 to 30 days
x: The draft cut the public notice period from 30 to 20 days, not the other way.

s: Which authority clears Category A projects under the EIA notification?
x: Category A projects are cleared by the MoEFCC at the Centre; Category B by the State SEIAA.

s: Under the NGT Act of which year was the National Green Tribunal set up?
x: The NGT Act was passed in 2010 and came into force on 18 Oct 2010.

s: Where is the Principal Bench of the National Green Tribunal located?
x: The Principal Bench is at Delhi; Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai are zonal benches.

s: Which of the following is NOT a zonal bench of the National Green Tribunal?
x: The zonal benches are Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai; Hyderabad is not one.

s: Which body did the National Green Tribunal replace?
x: The NGT replaced the National Environment Appellate Authority.

s: The NGT hears civil cases on substantial environmental questions under how many Acts listed in Schedule I?
x: Schedule I of the NGT Act lists 7 Acts.

s: GDP at market prices is ₹110; Indians earn ₹20 abroad, foreigners ₹10 in India; depreciation ₹15; net indirect taxes ₹5. What is the national income?
x: NFIA +10 gives GNP 120; minus depreciation 15 gives NNP 105; minus NIT 5 gives NI 100.

s: Which item is deducted from NNP at market prices to obtain national income?
x: National income is NNP at factor cost = NNP at market prices minus (indirect taxes minus subsidies).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. National income is NNP at factor cost.
2. National income is equal to NDP at factor cost plus NFIA.
3. National income is GDP at market prices.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: National income = NNP at factor cost = NDP at factor cost + NFIA; GDP at market prices is a different, wider aggregate.

s: Which of the following combinations represents the components of national income at factor cost?
o: Indirect taxes, subsidies, depreciation and exports
Consumption, investment, government expenditure and imports
Wages, rent, interest and profits earned by the country's normal residents
Only wages and salaries earned within domestic territory
x: National income is the sum of wages, rent, interest and profits earned by factors belonging to the country, including the adjustment for NFIA.

s: What kind of concept is national wealth, measured at a point of time?
x: National wealth is a stock measured at a point of time; national income is a flow measured over a period.

s: A country has GDP at market prices of ₹500 crore, depreciation of ₹50 crore, NFIA of –₹10 crore and net indirect taxes of ₹40 crore. What is its national income?
x: GNPMP = 500 – 10 = ₹490 crore; NNPMP = 490 – 50 = ₹440 crore; NNPFC = 440 – 40 = ₹400 crore. NNP at factor cost is national income.

s: A country's nominal GDP rises from ₹1,000 crore to ₹1,200 crore, while its price index rises from 100 to 120. What happens to its real GDP?
x: The increase in nominal GDP is exactly matched by the increase in the price index from 100 to 120, so output measured at constant prices remains unchanged.

s: At which prices is real GDP measured?
x: Real GDP uses constant base-year prices, nominal GDP current prices; real growth shows true output growth.

s: Why does nominal GDP growth usually exceed real GDP growth?
o: Because of the rise in the price level (inflation)
Because of net factor income from abroad
x: Nominal GDP uses current prices, so its growth includes price rise; it exceeds real growth by roughly the inflation rate.

s: In 2025-26 (estimates, old series), India's nominal GDP growth was 8.0%. What was its real GDP growth?
x: Real growth was 7.4%; nominal growth exceeds real growth by roughly the inflation rate.

s: What is the base year of India's new GDP series released on 27 February 2026?
x: The new series has base 2022-23, replacing 2011-12.

s: Under the new GDP series (base 2022-23), what was India's GDP at current prices in 2024-25?
x: The new series gives Rs 261.18, 289.84 and 318.07 lakh crore for 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25.

s: What is the investment multiplier (k) equal to?
x: k = 1/(1 − MPC), which is the same as 1/MPS.

s: With whom is the accelerator principle linked?
x: The accelerator, induced investment over the change in income, is linked to J.M. Clark.

s: What is investment that is independent of income, driven by a new product, technique or market, called?
x: Autonomous investment does not depend on income; induced investment rises with income.

s: If gross investment only covers depreciation, what is net investment?
x: Net investment = gross investment − depreciation, so it is zero.

s:
Consider the following statements about saving and investment:
1. Realised investment equals planned plus unplanned investment.
2. Equilibrium income is where planned saving equals planned investment.
3. If planned saving exceeds planned investment, output and income rise.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; excess planned saving piles up unsold goods, so output and income fall.

s: On what does the accelerator principle depend?
x: The accelerator links induced investment to the change in income, not its level; the multiplier works on MPC/MPS.

s: If the marginal propensity to save (MPS) is 0.25, what is the value of the investment multiplier?
Which one of the following conditions is necessary for per capita income to rise?
o: Income must grow more slowly than population
Depreciation must be greater than income growth
Income must grow faster than population
x: Per capita income rises only when the growth of income exceeds the growth of population.

s: What is deducted from personal income to obtain personal disposable income?
o: Undistributed corporate profits and social security contributions
Personal direct taxes and non-tax payments such as fines and fees
x: Personal disposable income equals personal income minus personal direct taxes and non-tax payments such as fines and fees.

s: Which of the following is ADDED to national income in arriving at personal income?
x: Transfer payments are added; undistributed profits, social security contributions and corporate tax are deducted.

s: Which of the following is deducted from national income in arriving at personal income?
x: Undistributed corporate profits are deducted; transfer payments are added; personal direct taxes are deducted later for disposable income.

s: How is per capita income calculated?
x: Per capita income is national income divided by population; it rises only when income grows faster than population.

s: How are national savings obtained?
o: Personal income minus personal direct taxes
x: National savings = national disposable income − consumption.

s: What is the value of all final goods and services produced within the geographical boundaries of a country during a year, irrespective of who produces them, called?
x: GDP measures the market value of final goods and services produced within a country's geographical boundaries during a year, including production by residents and non-residents.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: GNP is GDP plus NFIA. NDP is GDP minus depreciation, and NNP is NDP plus NFIA.

s: Which one of the following correctly represents Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA)?
o: Exports minus imports of goods and services
Domestic factor income minus domestic consumption
Factor income paid abroad minus factor income received from abroad
Factor income received from abroad minus factor income paid abroad
x: NFIA is factor income received from abroad minus factor income paid abroad. It is added to GDP to obtain GNP.

s: To which aggregate of India does an Indian resident's factor income earned in Saudi Arabia contribute?
x: Factor income earned by an Indian resident abroad is excluded from India's domestic product but included in its national product.

s: India's GNP is usually lower than its GDP. What is the usual sign of its net factor income from abroad?
x: India's NFIA is usually negative, making GNP lower than GDP.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: GNP considers nationality or factor income.
GDP includes net factor income from abroad.
GDP refers to production within the country.
x: Option B is incorrect: GDP counts production inside the country's borders. Net factor income from abroad (NFIA) is added to get GNP, the measure based on nationality.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: GDP is based on production within a country's domestic territory.
GDP includes production by residents both within and outside the country.
GNP includes production by residents within and outside the country.
GNP is based on production by normal residents of a country.
x: Option B is incorrect: GDP is based on location and counts all production inside the country. Counting residents' production inside and outside the country is GNP.

s: Under which condition will GNP be greater than GDP?
o: When net factor income from abroad is negative
When net factor income from abroad is positive
When depreciation exceeds net indirect taxes
When net factor income from abroad is zero
x: GNP = GDP + NFIA, so GNP exceeds GDP only when NFIA is positive.

s: What is the full form of NFIA?
x: NFIA = Net Factor Income from Abroad, the factor income received from abroad minus that paid abroad.

s: Which of the following is GNP equal to?
x: GNP = NNP + depreciation; national income is NNP at factor cost.

s: Why is depreciation deducted while calculating net national or domestic product?
o: Because depreciation measures the income earned by foreign factors
Because depreciation is a direct tax on capital goods
Because depreciation represents transfer payments to households
Because output used merely to replace worn-out capital does not constitute new output
x: Depreciation, or consumption of fixed capital, is deducted because production used only to replace worn-out capital adds nothing new to the productive stock.

s: What is Net Domestic Product (NDP) equal to?
x: NDP = GDP − depreciation; GNP − depreciation gives NNP.

s: Which is India's nodal agency for purchasing power parity estimation under the International Comparison Program?
x: The World Bank is the global implementing agency and the NSO is India's nodal agency.

s: Why is India's PPP-based GDP much larger than its GDP measured at the market exchange rate?
o: Market exchange rates include transfer payments while PPP excludes them
India has higher domestic price levels than the United States and China
Prices are lower in India, so the same domestic output has greater purchasing power when compared internationally
PPP excludes services from GDP measurement
x: Lower prices in India make its output larger when valued using purchasing power parity than when converted at market exchange rates.

s: Which is the global implementing agency of the International Comparison Program for PPP?
x: The World Bank implements the ICP globally; NSO is India's nodal agency.

s: What is India's rank by PPP-based GDP (ICP 2021)?
x: India is 3rd by PPP GDP, after the USA and China.

s: In 2025, India became the world's fourth-largest economy by nominal GDP by overtaking which country?
x: India became 4th by nominal GDP in 2025 (about USD 4.18 trillion), overtaking Japan.

s: Which country had the highest per capita GNI (PPP) in 2024?
x: In 2024, Singapore had the highest per capita GNI at PPP.

s: According to the World Development Report 2000, which country had the highest per capita income?
x: WDR 2000 placed Luxembourg first, at $44,640 per capita.

s: On what basis is GDP compared across countries under purchasing power parity (PPP)?
o: Pricing a common basket of goods and services at each country's own prices
Converting GDP at market exchange rates
x: PPP prices a common basket at each country's own prices, removing price-level differences.

s: Under which programme of the UN Statistics Division are PPP estimates made?
x: PPPs are estimated under the International Comparison Program of the UNSD; the World Bank is its global implementing agency.

s: According to the IMF World Economic Outlook (April 2026), what was India's rank by nominal GDP?
x: The IMF WEO April 2026 placed India 6th by nominal GDP (USD 4.15 trillion).

s: How is GDP at factor cost obtained from GDP at market prices?
x: Indirect taxes and subsidies, not direct taxes, bridge GDP at market prices and at factor cost.

s: Which of the following is a production tax rather than a product tax?
o: Sales tax on each unit sold
Excise duty per unit of output
x: Production taxes are levied irrespective of the quantity of output; stamp duty and property tax are examples. GST, excise and sales tax are product taxes levied per unit or value of product.

s: Which of the following is a product tax?
x: Product taxes such as GST and excise are levied per unit; land revenue, stamp duty and property tax are production taxes.

s: While converting GDP at market prices to GDP at factor cost, what is done with subsidies?
x: FC = MP − indirect taxes + subsidies, so subsidies are added back.

s: Which one of the following is NOT treated as a transfer payment for purposes of national income accounting?
x: Commission on resale is payment for a productive service and is included. Pensions, scholarships and unemployment allowances are transfer payments.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Value added at each stage — included without counting the full value of intermediate goods again
Intermediate goods — included separately in national income to reflect all production
Second-hand sales — included as current production in national income
Interest on public debt — factor payment for current productive services
x: Value added at each stage is included, while intermediate goods are excluded separately to avoid double counting. Second-hand sales and interest on public debt are also excluded in the stated accounting treatment.

s: Interest on public debt is excluded from national income because it is treated as what?
o: A transfer, not a factor payment
x: Interest on public debt, like tax revenue, is a transfer and not a factor payment.

s: Which of the following is excluded from national income because it is not a payment for factor services?
x: Transfer earnings are not payments for factor services; rent, productive interest and profit are factor incomes.

s: Which of the following is included in national income?
x: Commission on resale pays for a productive service; second-hand sales and transfer payments are excluded.

s: What does GVA at factor cost plus net production taxes give?
x: Adding net production taxes to GVA at factor cost gives GVA at basic prices; adding net product taxes then gives GDP.

s: GDP is equal to GVA plus which of the following?
x: GVA is the production-side measure; GDP is the wider measure, GVA plus taxes on products minus subsidies.

s: Why is a base year used in Real GVA?
o: remove the effect of price changes
x: Real GVA uses constant base-year prices to strip out price changes; nominal GVA uses current prices.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Gross Value Added (GVA)?
o: GVA at basic prices has been the headline sectoral measure since the 2011-12 series.
GVA at basic prices is not used in the 2022-23 series.
x: GVA at basic prices continues to be used in the 2022-23 series.

s: Which of the following is true of GVA and NVA?
o: GVA excludes depreciation; NVA includes it
GVA includes depreciation; NVA excludes it
x: GVA includes depreciation, while NVA excludes it.

s: In Q1 2026-27, real GDP was Rs 81.36 lakh crore and real GVA Rs 73.82 lakh crore. What does the difference between them represent?
x: GDP = GVA + taxes on products − subsidies, so the gap is net product taxes.

s: As per the AP Socio-Economic Survey, what is the value of all goods and services produced within the State in a period, counted without duplication, called?
x: This is the APSES definition of State Domestic Product. GNP is a national, nationality-based measure, and per capita income divides income by population.

s: On the basis of which aggregate is per capita income computed in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) at the national level
x: Andhra Pradesh per capita income is computed on the basis of Net State Domestic Product (NSDP).

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's per capita income in 2024-25 (FAE)?
x: AP's per capita income was Rs. 2,68,653 against India's Rs. 2,00,162 in 2024-25 FAE.

s: Which State has the highest per capita income among Indian States?
x: Goa has the highest per capita income among Indian States.

s: What was India's per capita income in 2024-25 (FAE)?
x: India's per capita income in 2024-25 (FAE) was Rs 2,00,162, against AP's Rs 2,68,653.

s: Which State is the largest State economy of India by GSDP (2024-25)?
x: Maharashtra has the largest GSDP among Indian States (2024-25); Tamil Nadu is second.

s: Which State ranked second by GSDP in India in 2024-25, after Maharashtra?
x: Tamil Nadu is the second-largest State economy, behind Maharashtra (2024-25).

s: In the 2022–23 national accounts series, which method replaced single deflation for manufacturing and agriculture?
x: The 2022–23 series uses double deflation, which separately deflates output prices and input prices.

s: Which of the following is regarded as the most comprehensive measure of inflation in India?
x: The GDP deflator covers all goods and services in GDP (consumption, investment, government, exports), whereas WPI, CPI and CPI-IW price fixed baskets (APPSC-G2 2025 key).

s: What is obtained by dividing nominal GDP by real GDP and multiplying by 100?
x: GDP deflator = nominal GDP / real GDP x 100, i.e. GDP at current prices over GDP at constant prices.

s: What happens to the purchasing power of money when the GNP deflator rises?
x: A rising deflator means higher prices, so each rupee buys less: purchasing power of money falls.

s: Why is the GDP deflator regarded as the most comprehensive measure of inflation?
o: It covers all goods and services included in GDP
It is based on a fixed basket of goods
x: The GDP deflator covers all goods and services in GDP, while WPI and CPI use fixed baskets.

s: In the expenditure method, which of the following is aggregated to measure national income?
x: The expenditure method adds consumption, investment, government expenditure and net exports, represented by C + I + G + (X − M).

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Largest expenditure component of GDP – Government spending
Share of private consumption in GDP – about 39 per cent
Share of private consumption in GDP – about 59 per cent
High private consumption share – more exposure to global swings
x: Private consumption is about 59 per cent of GDP, the largest component, and makes India less exposed to global swings.

s: Which component of GDP by expenditure is the most volatile?
x: Business investment is the most volatile; private consumption is the largest.

s: Which of the following is an example of working capital?
x: Working capital, like petrol or yarn, is used up in one production cycle; a plough or a computer is fixed capital.

s: What was the share of gross fixed capital formation (GFCF) in India's GDP in Q1 2026-27?
x: In Q1 2026-27, GFCF rose to 34.3% of GDP from 31.4%.

s: By how much did India's real gross fixed capital formation (GFCF) grow in Q1 2026-27?
x: In Q1 2026-27, real GFCF grew 11.9% and its share rose to 34.3% of GDP.

s: What was the growth of private consumption in India in Q1 2026-27?
x: Private consumption grew 7.1% in Q1 2026-27, while real GFCF grew 11.9%.

s: Under the income method, national income sums compensation of employees, operating surplus and which other item?
x: The income method sums compensation of employees, operating surplus (rent, interest, profit) and mixed income.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Cost and accounting method — Final expenditure method
x: Cost and accounting method is not a recognised method of measuring national income. The expenditure method is also called the consumption-and-investment or final expenditure method.

s: Which of the following is NOT a method of measuring national income?
x: The three methods are product (value added), income and expenditure; Cost and Accounting is not one.

s: By what other name is the income method of measuring national income known?
x: The income method is also called the factor income or distributed share method.

s: How do the final product method and the value added method of measuring national income compare?
x: Both avoid double counting and give the same total.

s: What is the income earned by a factor of production for services rendered to the production unit called?
x: Factor income is what a factor (land, labour, capital, enterprise) earns for its services to production.

s: In the Economic Survey formula of the income method, GDP = compensation of employees + consumption of fixed capital + (taxes on production − subsidies on production) + which other item?
x: The income-method formula adds gross operating surplus to employee compensation, fixed capital consumption and net production taxes.

s: Which of the following is included in national income?
x: Changes in inventories are included; tax revenue, interest on public debt and housewives' unpaid services are excluded.

s: Which of the following is excluded from national income?
o: Farm output consumed by the producing household
x: Housewives' unpaid services are excluded; imputed rent and self-consumed farm output are included.

s: A second-hand car is sold through a dealer. Which part of this transaction is included in national income?
o: The original purchase price and the resale price together
The entire sale value of the car
Only the broker's or dealer's commission
Neither the sale value nor the commission
x: The second-hand good itself was counted when originally produced. In the resale, only the current service represented by the broker's or dealer's commission is included.

s: Which of the following is treated as a factor payment and is therefore included in national income?
o: Interest earned on a productive loan
Pension received by a retired employee
x: Interest on productive loans is a return to a factor of production and is included. Pensions, scholarships and gifts are transfer payments.

s: How is imputed rent of owner-occupied houses treated in national income?
o: Excluded, as it is not marketed
x: Imputed rent is included; interest on public debt is excluded.

s: Why is the purchase of shares and bonds excluded from national income?
x: Financial transactions like shares and bonds create no new production.

s: Which method measures GDP as domestic factor incomes minus transfer payments?
x: The income method adds factor incomes (wages, rent, interest, profit); transfer payments are kept out.

s: In the real flow of a two-sector circular flow model, in which direction do factor services move?
x: In the real flow, households provide factor services to firms, and firms provide goods and services to households.

s: In the circular flow of income, which of the following is an injection?
x: Injections are investment, government spending and exports; saving, taxes and imports are leakages.

s: In an open economy, which of the following represents the equilibrium condition for leakages and injections?
o: S + T + M = I + G + X
C + S + X = I + T + M
S + I + T = M + G + X
S + T + X = I + G + M
x: The three leakages are saving, taxes and imports, while the three injections are investment, government spending and exports.

s: Which of the following is a leakage in the circular flow of income?
x: Saving, taxes and imports are leakages; investment, government spending and exports are injections.

s: In which work did J.R. Hicks state that Net Social Product and Social Income are the same?
x: In The Social Framework, J.R. Hicks said Net Social Product equals Social Income, because production pays out factor incomes.

s: The Income Method is principally used in India for estimating income generated by which group of activities?
o: Trade, transport, banking, real estate and public administration
x: The income method is used for service activities such as trade, transport, banking, real estate, public administration and other services.

s: Through which of the following does the new national accounts series improve real GVA measurement?
x: The new series uses double deflation and volume extrapolation to estimate real GVA.

s: In India, to which sectors is the production (value added) method mainly applied?
x: Production method: agriculture and allied, mining, manufacturing; income method: services.

s: Which method is used in part for construction and as a cross-check in India?
x: The expenditure (commodity flow) method is used partly for construction, and PFCE data serve as a cross-check.

s: State Domestic Product is generally estimated at the State level by using which approach?
x: States estimate GSDP primarily through the production, or income-originating, approach.

s: What is the base year used for the APSES 2024-25 figures?
x: The APSES 2024-25 figures are presented at 2011-12 base prices.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about State income?
o: 'Income originating' is the value produced within the State's boundaries.
'Income originating' includes income earned by the State's residents abroad.
'Income accruing' adds residents' income earned in other States or abroad.
x: Residents' income from outside the State is part of income accruing, not income originating.

s: Which agency compiles the Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Directorate of Economics and Statistics, AP
x: The Directorate of Economics & Statistics compiles State Domestic Product in each State, including AP. NSO compiles national accounts, RBI handles monetary statistics, and the Planning Board does not compile GSDP.

s:
Consider the following statements about State income in Andhra Pradesh:
1. GSDP of Andhra Pradesh is compiled by the NSO.
2. AP's per capita income is based on NSDP.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: AP's GSDP is compiled by the Directorate of Economics and Statistics, AP, not the NSO; per capita income is based on NSDP.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the nine sectors used for computing the GSDP of Andhra Pradesh?
x: AP's 9 GSDP sectors include mining, construction and electricity, gas and water; tourism and culture is not a separate sector.

s: How is GSDP at market prices obtained from GVA at basic prices?
o: By adding product taxes and deducting product subsidies
By adding production taxes and deducting production subsidies
By adding net factor income from abroad
x: GVA at basic prices + product taxes − product subsidies = GSDP at market prices.

s: Which of the following are treated as production subsidies in State income estimates?
x: Production subsidies are apprentice and interest subsidies; production taxes are stamp duties and property taxes.

s: On what basis was national manufacturing GVA traditionally allocated among the States?
x: Manufacturing GVA used to be allocated to States by ASI shares; GST data is now also available.

s: In May 2026, MoSPI issued a uniform guideline for compiling Gross State Value Added (GSVA) with which base year?
x: MoSPI's May 2026 guideline sets GSVA on base 2022-23 for consistency with the national accounts.

s: What does the value added (product) method sum to measure national income?
o: the value added by every producing unit
x: The product method sums the value added by each producing unit, avoiding double counting.

s: What is value added at a particular stage of production equal to?
o: Value of output minus depreciation only
Value of output minus intermediate consumption
Value of output plus intermediate consumption
Intermediate consumption minus value of output
x: Value added is calculated as the value of output minus the value of intermediate consumption.

s: In national income accounting, what does change in inventories equal?
x: Change in inventories is production minus sales, and unsold production counts as output.

s: How is double counting in national income (cotton → cloth → garment) avoided?
o: Adding the gross sales of all producers
Counting only the final product or the value added at each stage
Counting only the value of intermediate goods
Excluding the value of the final product
x: Including only the final product, or summing the value added by the farmer, weaver and tailor, prevents the cotton being counted repeatedly.

s: To avoid double counting, which goods are left out of national income?
x: Only final goods are counted; intermediate goods are excluded.

s: Under double deflation in the 2022-23 series, what does real GVA equal?
o: Real output minus real intermediate consumption
Nominal output minus real intermediate consumption
x: Double deflation deflates output and inputs separately: real GVA = real output − real intermediate consumption.

s: Who associated the national dividend with the net aggregate of commodities and services produced annually by labour and capital acting on natural resources?
x: Marshall defined the national dividend in terms of the net aggregate of commodities and services produced by labour and capital acting on natural resources.

s: Whose definition of national income is based on consumption, i.e. services received by ultimate consumers?
x: Fisher's definition is consumption-based; Kuznets added net additions to capital stock and Pigou included income from abroad.

s: Who defined national income as the part of community income, including income from abroad, that can be measured in money?
x: Pigou's definition is a money measure and includes income from abroad.

s: Simon Kuznets defined national income as net output flowing to ultimate consumers or into what?
x: Kuznets: net output flowing to ultimate consumers or into net additions to capital stock.

s: Which economies does Pigou's definition of national income mainly suit?
x: Pigou's money-measure definition suits developed countries, where nearly everything is bought for money.

s: Which of the following is NOT a major difficulty in measuring national income in India?
o: A well-documented and fully accounted informal sector
Black money and parallel economic activity
x: The informal sector is difficult to measure because it often lacks proper accounts; a well-documented and fully accounted sector would not constitute the stated difficulty.

s: A person simultaneously works as a farmer and a weaver. This illustrates which difficulty in national-income measurement?
x: When individuals perform several occupations, classification of their output and income becomes difficult because occupational specialisation is absent.

s: What did the IMF review (Dec 2025) read the persistent gaps between production- and expenditure-side GDP in India as showing?
x: The IMF saw the persistent gaps as pointing to only partial capture of informal activity.

s: What is the use of Supply and Use Tables in the new national accounts series primarily intended to do?
o: Exclude the unorganised sector from national accounts
Reduce the discrepancy between production and expenditure estimates
Replace GSDP with per capita income
Increase the discrepancy between production and expenditure estimates
x: Supply and Use Tables are used to reconcile supply and expenditure data and thereby reduce the discrepancy between the two sides of GDP estimation.

s: Farm output kept for home use makes national income hard to measure because of which difficulty?
x: Self-consumption is part of the non-monetised economy.

s: What was the first official estimate of national income for 1948-49 reported by the National Income Committee?
o: National income Rs 7,610 crore and per capita income Rs 225
National income Rs 8,710 crore and per capita income Rs 49
National income Rs 8,710 crore and per capita income Rs 225
National income Rs 8,710 crore and per capita income Rs 76
x: The first official estimate reported national income for 1948-49 as Rs 8,710 crore and per capita income as Rs 225.

s: At what amount did William Digby estimate India's per capita income for 1899?
x: Digby's estimate for 1899 gave a per capita income of Rs 18; Rs 20 was Naoroji's figure.

s: What was India's per capita income according to Findlay Shirras's 1911 estimate?
x: Findlay Shirras estimated per capita income at Rs 49 in 1911.

s: In which year did the CSO publish the first official national income estimates (conventional series, base 1948-49)?
x: The CSO's first official estimates came in 1956; 1949 was the year the National Income Committee was set up and 1951 its first report.

s: Who gave the first scientific estimate of India's national income?
x: V.K.R.V. Rao gave the first scientific estimate (for 1925-29); Naoroji made the first attempt.

s: Who was the chairman of the National Income Committee set up in August 1949?
x: The National Income Committee (1949) was chaired by P.C. Mahalanobis, with D.R. Gadgil and V.K.R.V. Rao as members.

s: Who made the first attempt to estimate the national income of India?
x: Dadabhai Naoroji made the first attempt, estimating national income for 1867-68.

s: Who is the author of 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'?
x: Dadabhai Naoroji wrote Poverty and Un-British Rule in India, which carried his national income estimate.

s: In which year did the National Income Committee submit its first report?
x: The Committee, set up in August 1949 under P.C. Mahalanobis, gave its first report in 1951.

s: What per capita income did V.K.R.V. Rao estimate for India?
x: V.K.R.V. Rao's first scientific estimate put per capita income at Rs 76; Naoroji's was Rs 20 and Shirras's Rs 49.

s: What is the nature of the Chairperson and the four members of the National Statistical Commission (2006)?
x: The NSC has a part-time Chairperson and four part-time members; the CEO of NITI Aayog is ex officio.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: NSO — umbrella body for national accounts, IIP, CPI and surveys
State DES — national-level monetary policy authority
x: The NSO is the umbrella body for national accounts, IIP, CPI and surveys. State DES prepares State Domestic Product and state statistics, while ISI is autonomous under the ISI Act, 1959.

s: Which body is India's nodal agency for the International Comparison Programme (ICP)?
o: Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT
x: The NSO, which follows IMF-SDDS norms, is India's nodal agency for the ICP.

s: Under which of the following does the National Statistical Office (NSO), formed in 2019, function?
o: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
x: The NSO (CSO + NSSO, 2019) is under MoSPI and headed by the Chief Statistician of India.

s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the National Statistical Office (NSO)?
o: Conduct of surveys such as PLFS, ASUSE and HCES
x: Monetary policy is not an NSO function; national accounts, IIP, CPI and surveys are.

s: Which body conducts the Annual Survey of Industries (ASI)?
x: The Kolkata wing conducts the ASI; ESD compiles IIP and the National Accounts Division handles GDP.

s: Who is the head of the National Statistical Office (NSO)?
x: The Chief Statistician of India heads the NSO and is also Secretary, MoSPI.

s: When was the Central Statistical Organisation (CSO) formed?
x: The CSO was formed on 2 May 1951; it merged with the NSSO in 2019 to form the NSO.

s: Which two bodies were merged in 2019 to form the National Statistical Office (NSO)?
x: The NSO was formed in 2019 by merging the CSO and the NSSO under MoSPI.

s: Which division of the CSO compiles the Index of Industrial Production (IIP)?
x: The Economic Statistics Division compiles the IIP; the National Accounts Division compiles GDP.

s: Who founded the Indian Statistical Institute in 1931?
x: P.C. Mahalanobis founded the ISI (1931) and the NSS (1950) and designed India's statistical system.

s: Under which Act is the Indian Statistical Institute an autonomous body?
x: The ISI is an autonomous institute under the ISI Act, 1959.

s: Who set up the National Sample Survey (NSS) in 1950?
x: P.C. Mahalanobis, architect of India's statistical system, founded the ISI (1931) and the NSS (1950).

s: Who is an ex officio member of the National Statistical Commission (2006)?
x: The NSC has a part-time Chairperson, 4 part-time members and the CEO of NITI Aayog ex officio.

s: Which IMF data standard does India's National Statistical Office follow?
x: The NSO follows the IMF's Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS).

s: Which base year of India's National Accounts immediately followed 1993-94?
x: The sequence runs 1980-81, 1993-94, 1999-2000, 2004-05; 2009-10 was never a base year.

s: In national income accounting, what are the prices of the base year used for?
o: Measure only the volume of exports
Determine the annual rate of population growth
Calculate only nominal GDP at current prices
Value real GDP at constant prices
x: The base year is the reference year whose prices are used to value real GDP at constant prices. For an index, the base year is generally assigned a value of 100.

s: What is the base year of the new Consumer Price Index (CPI) series?
x: The CPI was rebased to 2024 from the calendar year 2012; it is the IIP, not the CPI, that moved to 2022-23.

s: Which of the following was never a base year of India's national accounts?
x: 2009-10 was never a base year; the others are part of the sequence.

s: Counting up to the 2022-23 series, how many base years have India's National Accounts Statistics had?
x: The nine base years run from 1948-49 to 2022-23.

s: If national income at current prices is Rs 30,000 crore and the price index (base year = 100) is 150, what is the real national income?
x: Real income = current income x 100 / price index = 30,000 x 100 / 150 = Rs 20,000 crore.

s: What was the first inflation print of the new CPI series (base 2024), for January 2026?
x: The new CPI series released in February 2026 gave a first print of 2.75% for January 2026.

s: What was the headline measure of value added under the 2011-12 national accounts series?
x: The 2011-12 series adopted GVA at basic prices as the headline measure.

s: Under the 2011-12 series, which corporate database partly replaced the ASI for estimating the corporate sector?
x: The MCA-21 company database (1,35,802 companies) partly replaced the ASI (67,649 factories).

s: The 2011-12 base year series of India's national accounts, released in 2015, replaced which earlier base year?
x: The 2011-12 series replaced the 2004-05 base (APPSC 2017, 2019, 2023). 1999-2000 and 1993-94 are older bases; 2009-10 was never a base year.

s: Which organisation prepares estimates of consumption, capital formation and saving with institutional-sector detail?
o: State DES through GSDP accounts only
DPIIT through the Office of the Economic Adviser
x: MoSPI/NSO prepares estimates of consumption, capital formation and saving with institutional-sector detail.

s: With estimates of what is the K.N. Raj Committee (1981) associated?
x: The K.N. Raj Committee (1981) relates to saving and capital formation estimates.

s: As per NAS 2025, what was household saving as a share of GDP in 2023-24?
x: Household saving fell from 18.6% (2022-23) to 18.1% of GDP (2023-24).

s: What was private corporate investment as a share of GDP in India in FY24?
x: Private corporate investment was 11.2% of GDP in FY24; household saving was 18.1%.

s: Which body compiles the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) in India?
o: Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT
x: WPI is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT, not the NSO.

s: Which bodies release data on capital formation in India?
x: Capital formation estimates come from the RBI and the NSO.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Index of Industrial Production (IIP)?
o: It is released monthly, on the 28th
It covers mining, manufacturing and electricity
It is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT
x: The IIP is released by the NSO (compiled by the CSO's ESD); the OEA, DPIIT compiles the WPI.

s: The 2022-23 base year series of national accounts follows which edition of the United Nations System of National Accounts?
x: The 2022-23 series follows the United Nations System of National Accounts, 2025 edition.

s: Which of the following was a major criticism of the 2011-12 national accounts series?
o: It abandoned GVA as a measure of value added
It showed unusually high manufacturing growth that did not match physical indicators
It used only household survey data for manufacturing
It completely excluded the private corporate sector
x: The series was criticised for unusually high manufacturing growth that was inconsistent with physical indicators and for overestimating the private corporate sector.

s: According to former Chief Economic Adviser Arvind Subramanian, what was India's GDP growth during 2011-17 under the 2011-12 series?
x: Subramanian estimated growth at about 4.5% rather than the official ~7%, arguing that the series overstated it. 2.5% and 9% match neither his estimate nor the official one.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four institutional sectors in the 2022-23 national accounts series?
x: The four institutional sectors are government, public corporations, private corporations and households.

s: Which of the following correctly states the revised growth figures for 2023-24 and 2024-25?
o: 2023-24 was revised from 9.2% to 7.2%, while 2024-25 was revised from 6.5% to 7.1%
2023-24 was revised from 7.2% to 9.2%, while 2024-25 was revised from 7.1% to 6.5%
Both years were revised downward by 2 percentage points
Both years were revised upward by 0.6 percentage points
x: The 2023-24 growth estimate was cut from 9.2% to 7.2%, whereas the 2024-25 estimate was raised from 6.5% to 7.1%.

s: Why was 2022-23 considered a suitable base year for the revised national accounts series?
o: It was selected because base years cannot be revised after five years.
It was the first year in which India adopted the 2008 SNA.
It represented the peak of the COVID-related economic contraction.
It was unaffected by the GST transition, the COVID period and the immediate base effects of 2021-22.
x: 2022-23 was treated as a relatively normal year; 2017-18 involved the GST transition, 2019-21 was affected by COVID, and 2021-22 carried base effects.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the national accounts series with base year 2022-23?
o: It raised the size of nominal GDP for 2022-23 over the old series.
It uses double deflation for manufacturing and agriculture.
It integrates Supply and Use Tables.
It was released by the NSO, MoSPI on 27 February 2026.
x: The new series cut GDP by 3-4%: nominal 2022-23 GDP fell from about Rs 269 to Rs 261 lakh crore.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 2022-23 national accounts series:
1. It uses double deflation and Supply and Use Tables.
2. Private final consumption is benchmarked on HCES 2022-23.
3. It revised 2023-24 growth upward from 7.2% to 9.2%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; 2023-24 growth was revised down from 9.2% to 7.2%.

s: In the 2022-23 series, to what figure was the nominal GDP of 2022-23 revised from Rs 269 lakh crore?
x: The new series cut 2022-23 nominal GDP from Rs 269 to Rs 261 lakh crore, a cut of 3-4%.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Index of Industrial Production – created in 2019
Labour and employment data – Periodic Labour Force Survey
x: Labour and employment data come from the Periodic Labour Force Survey. The IIP is released monthly, the NSO was created in 2019 and GDP is part of the national income estimates.

s: In the estimation of the household or unincorporated sector, which of the following methods is used?
o: It is estimated exclusively from MCA-21 company filings
It is benchmarked on ASUSE and extrapolated using indicators
It is estimated only through PLFS employment data
It is benchmarked on the ASI and extrapolated using CPI
x: The household or unincorporated sector is benchmarked on ASUSE and subsequently extrapolated with suitable indicators. MCA-21 covers companies, while PLFS provides employment data.

s: Which of the following issues has been identified in current debates concerning national accounts?
o: The discontinuation of ASUSE and PLFS
The replacement of CPI-IW by GSDP
The abolition of all institutional-sector estimates
Coverage of the informal sector and MCA-based manufacturing GVA
x: Current criticism and debate concern the coverage of the informal sector and the use of MCA-based manufacturing GVA. IMF data concerns have also been raised.

s: Which survey is specifically associated with employment, unemployment, labour force participation rate and worker population ratio?
x: PLFS measures employment, unemployment, LFPR and WPR through monthly, quarterly and annual estimates.

s: At what frequency has the PLFS provided all-India labour estimates from 2025?
x: PLFS 2025 provides monthly all-India estimates, not only annual ones.

s: What does the ASUSE survey cover?
x: ASUSE covers unincorporated non-agricultural enterprises; ASI covers registered factories, HCES consumption and TUS time use.

s: Which NSO survey provides CPI weights and the benchmark for private final consumption?
x: The Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES) gives CPI weights and the PFCE benchmark.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: ASI covers registered factories; PLFS measures employment, ASUSE unincorporated enterprises and TUS time use.

s: To which year does the first full Household Consumption Expenditure Survey since 2011-12 relate?
x: HCES 2022-23 is the first full survey since 2011-12; the 2017-18 survey was withheld.

s: From when is population enumeration for India's delayed Census scheduled?
x: Houselisting runs April-September 2026 and population enumeration begins in February 2027.

s: Among the NSO's national income estimates, which comes immediately after the Second Advance Estimate?
x: The sequence is First Advance, Second Advance, Provisional, then First, Second and Third Revised Estimates.

s: When is the First Advance Estimate of national income generally released?
o: The last working day of May of the following year
7 June of the same financial year
Early January of the same financial year
End-February of the following financial year
x: The First Advance Estimate is released in early January of the same financial year.

s: Which method is primarily used to prepare advance estimates of national income?
x: Advance estimates use the benchmark-indicator method, which projects the relevant aggregates using available indicators.

s: When are quarterly GDP estimates generally released?
o: On the last working day of May irrespective of the quarter
One year after the quarter ends
At the beginning of January of the same quarter
Two months after the quarter ends
x: Quarterly GDP estimates are released about two months after the quarter ends; for example, Q1 2026-27 figures come at the end of August.

s: With effect from 2026, to which date was the release of the Provisional Estimate shifted?
x: The Provisional Estimate, earlier released on the last working day of May, was shifted to 7 June from 2026 after consultation with ACNAS.

s: At the end of which month is the Second Advance Estimate (SAE) of national income released?
x: The SAE comes at the end of February, after the FAE in early January.

s: From which data are quarterly GDP estimates mainly compiled?
o: Annual Survey of Industries results alone
x: Quarterly GDP uses high-frequency indicators and GST data and comes about two months after the quarter.

s: What was India's growth rate for 2025-26 in the Second Advance Estimate (new series)?
x: The SAE (end-February) put FY26 growth at 7.6% in the new series; the FAE had 7.4%.

s: The Directorate of Economics and Statistics, Andhra Pradesh, estimates GSDP in how many sectors?
x: DES Andhra Pradesh estimates GSDP in nine sectors.

s: Which base year does the Andhra Pradesh Socio-Economic Survey (APSES) still use for its GSDP estimates?
x: APSES still uses 2011-12 as the base year for GSDP. Statements that AP uses 2019-20 are a trap.

s: What is the 2025-26 First Advance Estimate of Andhra Pradesh's GSDP?
x: The DES, AP placed the 2025-26 FAE of GSDP at Rs 17.62 lakh crore.

s: Which of the following correctly states the indicators reported for the first quarter of 2026-27?
o: Real GDP 10.3 per cent, real GVA 7.8 per cent and nominal GDP 8.2 per cent
Real GDP 8.2 per cent, real GVA 10.3 per cent and nominal GDP 7.8 per cent
Real GDP 7.8 per cent, real GVA 10.3 per cent and nominal GDP 8.2 per cent
Real GDP 7.8 per cent, real GVA 8.2 per cent and nominal GDP 10.3 per cent
x: The reported figures are 7.8 per cent for real GDP, 8.2 per cent for real GVA and 10.3 per cent for nominal GDP.

s: By how many times has India's nominal GDP at market prices increased since 1991?
x: India's nominal GDP at market prices grew almost twelve times since 1991.

s: Which one of the following pairs of years and causes of contraction is correctly matched?
x: The contraction in 1979-80 was associated with drought and an oil shock. The contraction in 2020-21 was associated with COVID-19, while 2021-22 recorded a sharp rebound.

s: What was India's real GDP growth for 2023-24 as per the provisional estimates released in 2024?
x: 2023-24 growth was first printed as 8.2% (later 9.2% in the old series and 7.2% in the new series). 6.5% is the old-series 2024-25 figure, 7.1% the new-series 2024-25 figure and 7.8% the Q1 2026-27 figure.

s: What was India's GDP growth rate in 1950-51?
x: India's GDP grew by about 3.6% in 1950-51, close to the later 'Hindu rate of growth' of about 3.5%.

s: In which of the following years did India's real GDP contract because of drought and the oil shock?
x: India's GDP contracted in 1979-80 due to drought and the oil shock; the other contraction was 2020-21 (COVID-19).

s: What was India's real GDP growth for 2025-26 according to the Provisional Estimates released on 5 June 2026?
x: The FAE was 7.4% and the SAE 7.6%; the Provisional Estimates of 5 June 2026 put it at 7.7%.

s: What was the growth of agriculture in India in 2025-26?
x: Agriculture grew 3.1% in 2025-26, down from 4.6% the year before.

s: Which base year did the GDP series used for the first estimate of 2014-15 growth (released in 2015) adopt?
x: The 2014-15 growth of about 7.3% was the first estimate on the new 2011-12 base series (2015).

s: Which group consists only of States/UTs stated to have crossed the upper-middle-income threshold?
x: Karnataka, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat and Delhi crossed the threshold; Kerala is not in the list.

s: Andhra Pradesh ranked what position in India by GSDP, with its 2025-26 current-price GSDP estimated at ₹17.62 lakh crore?
x: Andhra Pradesh ranked eighth by GSDP, with a 2025-26 current-price GSDP of ₹17.62 lakh crore.

s: The Gini coefficient of per capita incomes across Indian States moved from 0.230 in 1994-95 to 0.261 in 2025-26. This indicates:
o: a fall in national per capita income
x: A rising Gini means greater inequality, so State incomes have diverged. Convergence would need a falling Gini; the figures plainly changed; the Gini says nothing about the level of national income.

s:
Consider the following about the 16th Finance Commission:
1. It introduced a contribution criterion based on the square root of GSDP.
2. It reduced devolution to 25 percent.
3. It retained the per capita GSDP income-distance criterion.
Which of the above statements are correct?
x: The new contribution criterion uses the square root of GSDP and the income-distance criterion remains; devolution stays at 41 percent, not 25 percent.

s: Among the four largest State economies, which grew fastest since 2021-22?
x: Karnataka grew fastest (about 65%); Maharashtra grew slowest of the big four.

s:
Consider the following statements about the EAC-PM report on States (Sep 2024):
1. Telangana's share of national GDP rose from 3.8% in 2010-11 to 4.9% in 2023-24.
2. Andhra Pradesh's share was about 4.7%, broadly flat after bifurcation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct as per 'Relative Economic Performance of Indian States: 1960-61 to 2023-24'.

s: Per the EAC-PM report, Andhra Pradesh's per capita income in 2023-24 was what % of the national average?
x: AP's relative PCI was 131.6%; 193.6% was Telangana's.

s: As per the 2025-26 FAE, Andhra Pradesh's per capita income is about how many times India's?
x: AP's PCI is about 1.34 times the all-India figure.

s: What GSDP does Swarna Andhra @2047 target for Andhra Pradesh?
x: The vision targets a GSDP of USD 2.4 trillion (about ₹308 lakh crore) by 2047.

s: What per capita income does Swarna Andhra @2047 target for Andhra Pradesh?
x: The target PCI is about USD 42,000 (₹55 lakh) by 2047.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Swarna Andhra @2047?
o: It targets a per capita income of about USD 42,000
It is built on the Ten Guiding Principles (P4 Padi Sutralu)
x: The vision targets 15% growth a year; 10.75% is AP's 2025-26 GSDP growth.

s: Which State had the largest economy by GSDP in India in 2024-25?
x: Maharashtra is India's largest State economy, followed by Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Gujarat.

s: According to the EAC-PM report (2024), which among the following had the highest relative per capita income in 2023-24?
x: The EAC-PM report placed Delhi at the top in relative per capita income, followed by Telangana, Karnataka and Haryana.

s: Which State was the second-largest economy by GSDP in India in 2024-25?
x: In 2024-25 Maharashtra was 1st by GSDP and Tamil Nadu 2nd, followed by Karnataka and Gujarat.

s: Who among the following is an author of the EAC-PM report 'Relative Economic Performance of Indian States: 1960-61 to 2023-24'?
x: The September 2024 EAC-PM report was written by Sanjeev Sanyal and Aakanksha Arora.

s: According to the EAC-PM report (2024), what was Telangana's relative per capita income in 2023-24 as a share of the national average?
x: Telangana's relative PCI was 193.6% of the national average; Andhra Pradesh's was 131.6%.

s: What is the per capita income threshold for upper-middle income that Karnataka, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat and Delhi have crossed?
x: These States/UTs crossed the upper-middle-income threshold of USD 4,636; India's figure is USD 2,760.

s: Under the World Bank's GNI per capita (Atlas method) classification, in which group is India placed?
x: India remains a lower-middle-income economy by the World Bank's Atlas-method GNI per capita classification, updated each 1 July.

s: What was India's rank in the world by nominal GDP after it overtook Japan in 2025?
x: India ranked fourth by nominal GDP after overtaking Japan in 2025, when its nominal GDP was stated as USD 4.18 trillion.

s: What is India's rank in the world by GDP measured at purchasing power parity?
x: India is the 3rd largest economy by PPP GDP, after the United States and China (ICP 2021); by nominal GDP it is 4th.

s: By which year is India projected to become the world's third-largest economy?
